title.rendered: He Who Calls You Is Faithful: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: He will do it. Paul closes his instructions not with more commands but with a promise. The One who called you is faithful. Your transformation is not a project you manage. It is a work He performs. Rest in His faithfulness, not your consistency.

content.rendered:
The Gospel For Today | Thursday, May 14, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do it.”
1 Thessalonians 5:24 (NIV) | ESV

Today’s Message

Four words carry everything in this verse: he will do it.

Paul has just finished a dense passage of instruction about how to live the Christian life, and then he lands here. He does not close with more commands. He closes with a promise. He does not say you must do it, you should do it, you need to try harder to do it. He says the One who called you is faithful, and He will do it.

The “it” refers to the work of sanctification and completion in your life. The transformation that God began in you when He called you is not your responsibility to complete in your own strength. It is His. He called you. And He is faithful. Those two facts together guarantee the outcome.

This is the same truth Paul expressed in Philippians 1:6, that He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus. The One who starts things is the One who finishes them. Your transformation is not a project you manage. It is a work He performs.

What does this mean practically? It means that when you feel like you are not making progress, when the same struggles seem to keep returning, when you wonder if you will ever become the person God has called you to be, the answer is not more willpower. The answer is trust. He called you. He is faithful. He will do it. Your confidence rests not in your consistency but in His.

Prayer

Father, I rest today in the truth that You will complete what You began in me. I am not responsible for finishing myself. You called me and You are faithful. I release the pressure I have been putting on myself to manufacture transformation in my own strength. I trust You with the outcome of my life. In Jesus name. Amen.

Declaration

The One who called me is faithful and He will do it. The work God began in me He will carry to completion. I am not responsible for finishing myself. He started this and He will see it through. I rest in His faithfulness today, not in my own consistency.
